answer.generated: Error-correcting output codes (ECOC) improves predictive performance by decomposing the original complex classification task into a series of simpler subtasks, each handled by a distinct base learner. This reduction in complexity often leads to easier learning, allowing each subtask to be addressed more effectively. By combining the outputs of these learners through majority voting or other strategies, the final prediction becomes more robust and accurate, even when the individual subtasks are imperfect. Thus, ECOC transforms a potentially intractable problem into a set of manageable pieces, enabling better overall classification outcomes.
